accepted_claims: If each interior p becomes extreme after removing at least one original hull vertex, an explicit fixed-edge injection gives ppt(S) >= product_p |E(p)| times t(S).
A certified six-point triangulation has no contained pointed pseudotriangulation; every universal containment-only injection or containment Hall argument fails.
For one interior point, every PPT has a unique triangulation refinement and ppt(S)=sum_T d_p(T), with d=3 for degree 3, d=2 for degree 4, and a degree-5 zero fiber.
For arbitrary S, ppt(S)=sum_T sum_{P contained in T} 1/R(P); the needed global average lower bound is unproved.
The displayed six-point wheel has an analytic count of t(S)=11 and ppt(S)=25, so it is no counterexample to the universal inequality.
remaining_gap: The sufficient-condition injection requires every interior point to have an original-hull exposure witness. Arbitrary point sets need not satisfy this. The refinement identity does not establish a global average of at least one, and individual fibers can be empty. The universal per-set ppt(S) >= t(S) conjecture remains unresolved by this work.
full_target: For every finite planar general-position point set S with n >= 3, pointed pseudotriangulations of S are at least as numerous as triangulations of the same S, with the full point set and no Steiner vertices.
